data.current_description:
The basic query API endpoint. Some browsers and proxies limit URL length. Send queries longer than 11 KB as a POST; `@sanity/client` switches to POST when the encoded query string reaches 11,264 characters.

Note: When a document is not found, GROQ still evaluates to a value. Thus, you don't get 404 errors through this endpoint.
Some examples:
* `*[_id == "missing"]` results in `[]`
* `count(*[_type == "typoType"])` results in `0`
* `*[_id == "missing"][0]` results in `null`
* `*[_id == "missing"][0].someProp` also results in `null`
data.summary_suggestion: Query Content Lake with GROQ via GET request
data.description_suggestion: Execute a GROQ query against the Sanity Content Lake using the GET method. This endpoint accepts query parameters including the GROQ query string, parameters, and options like perspective and explain. Returns a QueryResponse object containing the query results. Note: URL length is limited; queries exceeding 11 KB should be sent via POST instead. GROQ evaluates missing documents to empty arrays, zero counts, or null values rather than returning 404 errors, so all queries return 200 status with results in the response body.

data.current_description:
Use POST for long queries or large parameter values. `@sanity/client` sends queries as a POST when the encoded query string reaches 11,264 characters.
Queries sent using the POST method will also be cached on the CDN.

The request body only accepts `query`, `params`, and `returnQuery`. Pass other options, such as `perspective`, `explain`, `resultSourceMap`, and `tag`, as URL query parameters. Unknown body fields return a 400 error.
